pages.title: Tension Post
pages.text: Logs around a Binding Knot, Thread on top. Place it on the pad. Right-click it with a Strand token to **seat** that Strand. The notch lights, the tribe chimes, the pad changes.

pages.title: Knot, then seat
pages.text:
A **Strand token** is proof. You never craft one. You never spend one in a recipe.

Each Strand chapter in the assignment list ends in a **Knot** (hexagon). Tick it; the token drops. **Seat it** at the Post. Spares are souvenirs. Only the first seat counts.

Two of Clock, Swarm, or Spark seated, plus a Strand Filament on the Post: **Braid Cord**. All nine seated, plus a March stone: the **Spindle Loom Fragment**. Seat that too.

pages.title: A promise in public
pages.text:
A seated token is not fuel. It is a promise kept where the Clowder can hear it. The Post hums. The tribe chimes. The pad changes — hearth, footing, haste, luck — because nine agreements used to be a floor, and the Strand still remembers the trick.

Seat in order of the work, not in order of vanity. The Fray does not care who looked busy.

pages.title: What the Post is for
pages.text:
Near the Post: the pad mends you (Soil). It feeds you a little (Sprout). Fall damage stops within sight of it (Claw). Hands quicken (five Strands). Luck (Sigil). The horizon warms, one Strand at a time.

That is Loom Tension. It is not a bar. It does not nag. It is the sky noticing that someone is doing maintenance again.
